gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the makers' longevity and peak-power claims on one basis: BLUETTI rates the Elite 200 V2 at 6,000+ cycles to 80% of capacity, while Jackery's Explorer 2000 v2 is rated at 4,000 cycles to at least 70%. BLUETTI's 3,900 W 'Lifting Power' is for pure resistive loads only, not a surge rating like Jackery's 4,400 W or EcoFlow's 4,800 W. ALLPOWERS' own S2000 Pro + SP037 400 W kit listing says its polycrystalline panels convert 'about 60%', so 'a 100W solar panel can output about 55W-65W'.
standout_why: I compared against StormWatts (cited in both chats), Dealectric's own panels-included page (cited in chat 2) and Powersized's best-solar-generator page. StormWatts gives no AC, surge or cycle-life figures. It covers solar input caps and series or parallel wiring in depth (voltage, amps, Voc and Isc), so a wiring footnote would not stand out. Our own page lists rated vs measured Wh and continuous AC, but no cycle life, and its only surge figure is Jackery's. Powersized gives no cycle life or surge. None of the three mentions ALLPOWERS' own '55W-65W per 100W' panel statement.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. Among 2 kWh kits with 400 W of panels, the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 2×200 W has the strongest stated longevity on the stricter basis (6,000 cycles to 80%, against Jackery's 4,000 to 70%). Two cautions belong in the footnote. First, its 3,900 W figure only applies to resistive loads like kettles and hair dryers. For motor or compressor starts, compare Jackery's 4,400 W surge and EcoFlow's 4,800 W surge with BLUETTI's 2,600 W continuous, because BLUETTI's page gives no surge figure. Second, BLUETTI's Elite 200 V2 page reads 'expected to ship in early January for orders placed on or after Nov. 18', which conflicts with the Nov 26 dispatch date in our kit table, so the shipping column needs a re-check. Our ALLPOWERS 400 W kits that ship now are cheapest per Wh: R2500 V2 + SP037 at $913.49 is $0.476/Wh, and S2000 Pro + SP037 at $917.93 is $0.633/Wh. They come with one 400 W panel that the maker's own listing rates at about 55–65% real output. That stretches the R2500 V2 refill from 4.8 h of full sun at rated output to about 7.4–8.7 h, so they win on price per Wh, not on solar refill.
candidates: Jackery Solar Generator 2000 v2 (2× SolarSaga 200 W)
EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Solar Generator (2×220 W)

findings.label: Cycle life (stated basis)
findings.note: APH Networks quotes BLUETTI's spec sheet ('obtained from the manufacturer's website'). BLUETTI's US kit page and CA product page that I opened state no cycle life.

findings.label: AC rated output / peak figure
findings.value: 2,600 W continuous; Power Lifting up to 3,900 W for pure resistive loads only (kettles, electric blankets, hair dryers); no surge figure stated
findings.note: The US kit page https://www.bluettipower.com/products/elite-200-v2-2-sp200l states the same 2,600 W and the same 3,900 W resistive-only Power Lifting. Lifting is a reduced-voltage mode, not surge capacity, so 3,900 W can't be compared with Jackery's or EcoFlow's surge figures.

findings.label: Kit price and shipping note
findings.value: $1,499.00; Elite 200 V2 page reads 'expected to ship in early January for orders placed on or after Nov. 18'
findings.note: The price matches our kit table. The shipping note conflicts with the table's 'dispatch Nov 26' and needs a re-check before publishing. Data flag: our kit table shows 'AC 400 W' for this kit and for the AC180 + 2×200 W kit, which looks like panel watts entered in the AC column. BLUETTI states 2,600 W AC for the Elite 200 V2.

findings.label: Cycle life (stated basis)
findings.value: 4,000 cycles to at least 70% of original capacity
findings.source_title: This new Jackery power station charges in under two hours (T3, Matt Kollat, 2025-02-17)
findings.note: Jackery's own product pages returned HTTP 429 to every fetch. The end point is 70%, against BLUETTI's 80%, so the cycle counts are not on the same basis.

findings.label: Kit price, AC output, shipping note
findings.value: $1,239.00 (compare-at $1,899); 2,200 W continuous, 4,400 W surge; '200w Panel: Pre-order, ships by Nov 28'
findings.note: Read through the Shopify store tool's search of jackery.com. ChatGPT showed a range of $1,239–$1,649. The listing text doesn't confirm that the bundle contains 2×200 W panels.

findings.label: AC output / surge / X-Boost
findings.value: 2,400 W continuous; 4,800 W surge; X-Boost runs appliances up to 3,400 W
findings.note: Read through the store tool's search of us.ecoflow.com. EcoFlow gives surge and X-Boost as separate figures. Listed price $1,229.00 (compare-at $1,998), but the listing text doesn't name the panels in the bundle. ChatGPT's $1,429 matches the DELTA 3 Max Plus Solar Generator listing ($1,429), whose text says 'Pre-order: Ships in mid September' and 'High 400W solar input'.

findings.label: Maker's own statement on panel real output
findings.value: 'polycrystalline… conversion rate… about 60%. That is, a 100W solar panel can output about 55W-65W'; S2000 Pro takes '2* solar panel 200W in parallel (400W max)… 650W max'; 2,400 W AC (surge 4,000 W)
findings.source_title: ALLPOWERS Solar Generator Kit 2400W (S2000 Pro + SP037 400W Solar Panel)
findings.note: Read through the store tool's search of iallpowers.com (price $1,043.10, matching our table). The same text also claims 'up to 22% efficiency', so the '60%' is the maker's own loose wording, not a measurement. Arithmetic at the maker's 55–65%: 400 W gives about 220–260 W. Refilling 1,451 Wh takes 3.6 h of full sun at rated output, or about 5.6–6.6 h at 55–65%. Price per Wh at the link price: $917.93 / 1,451 Wh = $0.633/Wh.

findings.label: Kit specs as listed
findings.value: 1,920 Wh; 2,500 W AC; one 400 W SP037 panel; 1,000 W max solar input; 5-year warranty; no cycle count stated ('Long-lasting LiFePO4 battery')
findings.source_title: ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 + SP037 400W Solar Panel | 2500W Solar Generator Kit
findings.note: Price $1,038.05, matching our table. At the $913.49 link price: $0.476/Wh. Refill: 1,920 / 400 = 4.8 h of full sun at rated output, or about 7.4–8.7 h at the 55–65% that ALLPOWERS' own S2000 Pro listing states for its polycrystalline panels.

findings.label: Panel voltage
findings.value: 37.4 V (stated as the panel's output voltage); polycrystalline cells
findings.note: Standalone panel listed at $379.05. The S2000 + SP037 listing describes the same panel as 'polycrystalline… up to 22%'.

findings.label: Cycle life as listed (no end point)
findings.value: R3500: 'over 3,500 charging cycles'; S2000: 'ensures 1000+ life cycles'; neither says to what % of capacity
findings.source_title: ALLPOWERS Solar Generator Kit 3200W (R3500 + SP037 400W Solar Panel)
findings.note: R3500 kit listing: $1,803.10, 3,200 W AC (7,000 W peak). The S2000 wording comes from https://iallpowers.com/products/allpowers-s2000-solar-generator-portable-power-station-2000w-1500wh-with-sp037-400w-solar-panel (AC 2,000 W, peak 4,000 W). With no end point stated, these counts can't be put in the same column as BLUETTI's (80%) or Jackery's (70%).

unsourced: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max cycle life and its end point: EcoFlow's US product pages returned HTTP 429, and only a retailer's copy said '80%+ capacity after 4000 cycles' (thecabindepot.ca, not opened, not a maker source).
A surge figure for the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2: the US kit page and CA product page give only 2,600 W continuous and 3,900 W resistive-only Lifting Power.

Cycle life with an end point for the ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 and S2000 Pro: the US listings give no count (R2500 V2) or no % (S2000). An EU R2500 (2,016 Wh) sheet with 3,500+ to 80% is a different model, so I didn't use it.
SP037 Voc/Isc and the S2000 Pro's solar input voltage window: the iallpowers.com product pages returned HTTP 429 when I tried to open them in full.
Panel contents of EcoFlow's $1,229 'DELTA 3 Max Solar Generator' listing (which panels, how many): the listing text read through the store tool doesn't say.
Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 cycle life on Jackery's own page and its solar input spec: every jackery.com fetch returned HTTP 429.
Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 + 400 W: not researched within the call budget.
